methodology: Downloaded the USGS Geographic Names Information System (GNIS) 'Domestic Names' national text export (pipe-delimited, 981,698 feature records covering all 50 states, DC, and US territories). Read with UTF-8 encoding (file has a UTF-8 BOM, stripped via utf-8-sig). Matched feature_name against two word-boundary-anchored, case-insensitive regular expressions: DARK = \b(devil|devils|hell|hells|satan|demon|demons|hades|purgatory|diablo|diablos|inferno)\b, LIGHT = \b(angel|angels|paradise|eden|heaven|heavenly)\b. Word boundaries were verified to correctly exclude common substring false-positive risks (Shell, Mitchell, Angelina, Los Angeles, Edenton, Shelley, Rachel, Michelle) -- a full-file scan confirmed zero such names spuriously matched either regex. Only rows whose feature_class was in the natural-feature / settlement allow-list were kept (Stream, Summit, Valley, Lake, Spring, Canyon, Gap, Ridge, Basin, Cliff, Arch, Bar, Bend, Cape, Falls, Flat, Gut, Island, Lava, Pillar, Plain, Range, Rapids, Slope, Swamp, Woods, Area, Beach, Bench, Crater, Glacier, Isthmus, Populated Place); rows in the man-made exclude list (Church, School, Building, Cemetery, Hospital, Locale, Mine, Dam, Airport, Bridge, Canal, Crossing, Levee, Oilfield, Park, Post Office, Reservoir, Tower, Trail, Tunnel, Well, Harbor, Military) were dropped, as were matches in classes on neither list (Civil, Bay, Channel, Census, Arroyo -- administrative/hydrographic classes not covered by the spec). Coordinates came from prim_lat_dec / prim_long_dec (primary point location, decimal degrees). Rows with exact (0,0) coordinates were dropped as GNIS 'null island' placeholders for unlocated/historical-deprecated features (mirrors the same discipline applied to the FARS layer's sentinel-coordinate filtering). Remaining coordinates were rounded to 3 decimal places. Every kept row got v=1 (a name is a name; no weighting), with meta.side (dark/light), meta.class (feature_class), and meta.state (2-letter postal/territory abbreviation, derived from state_name).

source.name: USGS GNIS Domestic Names, National file

false_positive_check.method: Ran both regexes against 9 known substring-collision risk names (Shell, Mitchell, Angelina, Los Angeles, Edenton, Shelley, Rachel, Michelle, Purchell) directly, then scanned the full 981,698-row file for any feature_name containing the lowercase substrings 'shell','mitchell','angelina','angeles','edenton','rachel','michelle' that also matched either regex.
false_positive_check.result: Zero false-positive matches found across the entire national file for any of those substrings.
false_positive_check.manual_spot_check: Manually reviewed 20 random dark-side and 20 random light-side kept records (seeded random sample). All 40 were genuine on-topic matches (e.g. 'Devils Canyon', 'Hells Canyon', 'Purgatory Creek', 'Satan Butte' on the dark side; 'Paradise Valley', 'Eden', 'Angel Ridge', 'Heavenly Hollow' on the light side). No false positives required manual exclusion -- the word-boundary regex + class filter combination was sufficient on its own for this dataset.

caveats: 32 dark-side and light-side name matches nationally (out of 981,698 total rows in the file) had exact (0,0) placeholder coordinates -- e.g. 'Hell Town (historical)', 'Eden (historical)' -- typically deprecated/historical GNIS entries never assigned a real primary point. These were dropped from the layer rather than plotted at Null Island; this mirrors the FARS layer's discipline of dropping sentinel/placeholder coordinates.

'Canyon' is listed in the allow-list feature_class set per the task spec, but the current GNIS schema does not use 'Canyon' as a feature_class value at all (canyons are classified as 'Valley' or 'Gap' instead) -- so it produced zero matches, not a bug.

Classes 'Civil', 'Bay', 'Channel', 'Census', and 'Arroyo' had name matches but were on neither the keep nor exclude list in the spec, so they were dropped from the layer (184 rows total) rather than guessed into either bucket.

prim_lat_dec/prim_long_dec are GNIS's official point coordinate for the feature; for linear features like Stream or long Valley/Range names this is a single representative point (often the mouth/origin), not the full extent of the feature.

'Populated Place' entries with dark/light names (e.g. a town literally named 'Paradise' or 'Hell') are real, currently-recognized place names in GNIS, not slang or folklore labels; they are included per the settlement allow-list.

Two records fall in US territories rather than states: one 'Paradise' in the US Virgin Islands (state abbreviated VI) and one 'Paradise Island' in the U.S. Minor Outlying Islands (abbreviated UM, a remote Pacific atoll grouping, not a populated jurisdiction).

Feature names are historical GNIS entries and may reflect place names assigned decades or over a century ago; some may be considered offensive or archaic by modern standards (GNIS itself has been actively renaming a separate category of derogatory names, but the words matched here -- devil/hell/angel/paradise/etc. -- are not part of that renaming program).
